body.text: 1. What is Microsoft Excel?
Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet application developed by Microsoft. It is used to organize, calculate, analyze and visualize data efficiently.
Excel is widely used in schools, colleges, businesses, hospitals, banks and government organizations for maintaining records, preparing reports and performing calculations.
Microsoft Excel is one of the world's most widely used spreadsheet applications.
2. Workbook
A Workbook is an Excel file. It contains one or more worksheets. The default Excel file extension is .xlsx.
3. Worksheet
A Worksheet is a single spreadsheet page inside a workbook where users enter and organize data.
4. Rows and Columns
Rows run horizontally and are identified using numbers. Columns run vertically and are identified using letters.
5. Cell and Cell Address
A Cell is the intersection of a row and a column. Every cell has a unique address.
6. Ribbon
The Ribbon is the command area located at the top of Excel. It contains all tools required for working with worksheets.
7. Formula Bar
The Formula Bar displays the content or formula of the selected cell.
8. Name Box
The Name Box displays the address of the currently selected cell. You can also jump directly to any cell by typing its address.
9. Common Keyboard Shortcuts

body.title: How to Create and Save a New Workbook
steps: Click 'Blank Workbook' on the Start screen.
Click on a cell and note the change in the Name Box.
Press Ctrl + S to save the workbook.
Type a file name and click Save.

body.title: Practice Exercise - Explore the Excel Interface
steps: Identify and click on the Ribbon, Formula Bar, and Name Box.
Type your name into cell A1 and press Enter.
Use the Name Box to jump directly to cell D10.

body.text: Mastering these basics makes learning formulas, functions, charts, Pivot Tables and dashboards much easier.

chapters.title: Day 2: Data Entry, Editing, AutoFill and Flash Fill

concept.title: Entering, Editing and Managing Data in Microsoft Excel

body.text: 1. What is Data Entry?

Data Entry is the process of entering information into Microsoft Excel worksheets. Every piece of information entered into Excel is stored inside a cell. Excel supports different types of data such as text, numbers, dates, time, currency, percentages, and formulas.
Every value entered in Excel is stored in a cell identified by its unique cell address such as A1, B5, or C10.
2. Methods of Entering Data
There are several ways to enter data into Excel. The easiest method is to click a cell, type the required information, and press Enter.

rows: Type directly into the selected cell.
Type or edit data using the Formula Bar.
Paste data copied from another worksheet or application.
Import data from CSV, Text, or external databases.

body.text: 3. Editing Data
Editing means modifying existing data without deleting the entire worksheet. Excel provides several methods for editing cell contents.

items: Press F2 to edit the active cell.
Replace the existing value by typing a new value.

body.text: Editing data does not change the worksheet structure. It only changes the contents of the selected cell.
4. AutoFill
AutoFill is a powerful Excel feature that automatically fills cells with a series of values or copies existing values and formulas. It saves time by reducing repetitive typing.
Drag the small square (Fill Handle) located at the bottom-right corner of the selected cell to use AutoFill.

body.title: How to Use AutoFill
steps: Type the starting value(s) in a cell (e.g. 1 and 2 in two cells).
Hover over the small square (Fill Handle) at the bottom-right corner.
Click and drag down or across to fill the series.
Release the mouse to complete the fill.

body.text: 5. Flash Fill
Flash Fill automatically detects patterns in your data and fills the remaining cells without requiring formulas. It is commonly used to split names, combine text, or extract specific information.
Flash Fill recognizes patterns based on the examples you provide. It does not use formulas.

body.title: How to Use Flash Fill
steps: Type the desired output pattern in the first cell (e.g. just the first name).
Start typing the same pattern in the next cell.
Press Ctrl + E, or accept the suggested preview.
Verify the filled data is correct for every row.

body.text: 6. Difference Between AutoFill and Flash Fill

rows: Copies values, formulas or creates series

body.title: Practice Exercise - Student Marks Entry
steps: Create a worksheet with columns: Roll No, Student Name, Subject, Marks.
Use AutoFill to generate Roll Numbers from 1 to 20.
Enter 5 full names, then use Flash Fill to extract just the first names into a new column.
Copy a marks formula down all 20 rows using AutoFill.

body.text: 7. Best Practices

items: Always verify data after using Flash Fill.
Use AutoFill for repetitive numeric or date sequences.
Use Flash Fill for text formatting and extraction.
Use Undo (Ctrl + Z) if mistakes occur.
Data Entry is the process of entering information into Excel cells.
Editing allows existing data to be modified.
AutoFill copies values, formulas and creates series automatically.
Flash Fill recognizes patterns and fills data without formulas.
AutoFill and Flash Fill improve productivity and reduce manual work.

body.text: 1. What is Formatting?
Formatting is the process of changing the appearance of data without changing its actual value. It improves readability, makes reports attractive, and helps present information professionally.
2. Font Formatting
Font formatting changes the appearance of text inside a cell. You can change the font style, font size, make text Bold, Italic, Underline, and change the font color.

body.title: How to Change Font Color
steps: Select the cell or range of cells.
Click the Font Color (A) drop-down button.

body.text: Use dark colors for headings and bright colors only to highlight important information.
3. Cell Borders
Borders draw lines around cells to separate and organize data. They make tables easier to read.

body.title: How to Apply Borders
steps: Choose All Borders, Outside Borders, Thick Border, or another border style.

body.text: Use 'All Borders' for tables and 'Thick Outside Borders' for highlighting important sections.
4. Fill Color
Fill Color changes the background color of a cell. It is commonly used for headings, totals, warnings, and important information.

body.title: How to Apply Fill Color
steps: In the Font group, click the Fill Color (Paint Bucket) button.

body.text: Light colors improve readability. Avoid using too many different colors in the same worksheet.
5. Alignment
Alignment controls how text or numbers appear inside a cell. Data can be aligned horizontally or vertically.

body.title: How to Change Alignment
steps: Click Left, Center, or Right Alignment.
Use Top, Middle, or Bottom Align if required.

body.text: 6. Merge & Center
Merge & Center combines multiple adjacent cells into one cell and places the text in the center. It is commonly used for worksheet titles.
Avoid merging cells inside data tables because it may affect sorting and filtering.
7. Wrap Text
Wrap Text displays long text on multiple lines within the same cell instead of overflowing into adjacent cells.
8. Format Painter
Format Painter copies the formatting of one cell and applies it to another cell without copying the data.

rows: Wrap Text (Insert a new line within the same cell)

body.title: How to Use Format Painter
steps: Click or drag over the destination cells.

body.text: Double-click Format Painter to apply the same formatting to multiple locations.

body.title: Practice Exercise - Student Report Card
steps: Change the title font color to White.
Apply Blue Fill Color to the header row.
Apply All Borders to the table.
Merge and Center the worksheet title.
Use Wrap Text for long headings.
Use Format Painter to copy the formatting to another table.

chapters.title: Day 4: Number Formats, Dates, Time, Currency

concept.title: Formatting Numbers, Dates, Time and Currency in Microsoft Excel

body.text: 1. What is Number Formatting?
Number Formatting changes the appearance of numbers without changing their actual value. It helps present data in a professional and meaningful way.
Changing the number format does not change the value stored in the cell. It only changes how the value is displayed.
2. Number Format
The Number format displays numeric values with commas, decimal places, and negative number styles. It is commonly used for marks, quantities, salaries, and financial reports.

body.title: How to Apply Number Format
steps: Click the Number Format drop-down list.
Use Increase Decimal or Decrease Decimal to adjust decimal places.

body.text: 3. Date Format
Excel stores dates as serial numbers but displays them in different date formats. Date formatting makes reports easier to read.

body.title: How to Apply Date Format
steps: Select Short Date or Long Date.

body.text: Always store dates as real Excel dates instead of typing them as plain text.
4. Time Format
Time formatting is used to display hours, minutes, and seconds. Excel stores time as a fraction of a day.
5. Currency Format
Currency format displays monetary values with currency symbols such as ₹, $, or €. It is commonly used in salary sheets, invoices, and financial reports.

body.title: How to Apply Currency Format
steps: Choose Currency or Accounting from the Number Format list.

body.text: Accounting format aligns currency symbols and decimal points, making financial statements easier to read.
6. Percentage Format
Percentage format converts decimal values into percentages. It is commonly used for marks, attendance, discounts, growth rates, and profit calculations.
7. Increase & Decrease Decimal
Excel allows you to increase or decrease the number of decimal places displayed for numeric values.

body.title: How to Change Decimal Places
steps: Click Increase Decimal or Decrease Decimal.

body.text: 8. Format Cells Dialog Box
The Format Cells dialog box provides advanced formatting options such as Number, Alignment, Font, Border, Fill, and Protection.

body.title: How to Open Format Cells
steps: Select the required category and click OK.

body.title: Practice Exercise - Employee Salary Register
steps: Create a salary register with Employee ID, Employee Name, Joining Date, Basic Salary, HRA, Bonus, and Gross Salary.
Apply Number format to numerical columns.
Apply Currency format (₹) to salary columns.
Apply Date format to Joining Date.
Apply Percentage format to Bonus column.
Increase decimal places to two digits.
Use Accounting format for Gross Salary.

chapters.title: Day 5: Rows, Columns, Hide/Unhide, Freeze Panes

concept.title: Managing Rows, Columns and Worksheet Navigation

body.text: 1. Understanding Rows and Columns

Rows run horizontally and are identified by numbers (1, 2, 3...). Columns run vertically and are identified by letters (A, B, C...). Every worksheet consists of thousands of rows and columns where data is stored.
2. Insert and Delete Rows & Columns
Excel allows you to insert new rows or columns and delete unwanted ones without affecting the rest of the worksheet.
3. Adjust Row Height and Column Width
Resize rows and columns manually or automatically using AutoFit.

body.title: AutoFit Column Width
steps: Double-click the right border of the column header.

body.text: 4. Hide and Unhide Rows & Columns
Hide rows or columns temporarily without deleting data. Hidden data can be restored anytime.

body.title: Unhide a Column
steps: Select the columns on both sides.

body.text: Hidden data is still available in formulas and calculations.
5. Freeze Panes
Freeze Panes keeps selected rows or columns visible while scrolling through large worksheets.

body.title: Freeze the First Column
steps: View → Freeze Panes → Freeze First Column.

body.title: Freeze Both Rows and Columns
steps: Select the cell below the row and to the right of the column you want to freeze.

body.text: Freeze Panes is especially useful for attendance sheets, mark sheets, and large reports.

chapters.title: Day 6: Page Layout, Print Area, Headers and Footers

body.text: 1. Page Layout
The Page Layout tab allows you to control how your worksheet appears when printed. You can change margins, orientation, paper size, themes, and scaling.
2. Margins
Margins determine the blank space around the edges of a printed page.

body.title: Change Margins
steps: Choose Normal, Wide, Narrow or Custom Margins.

body.text: 3. Orientation and Paper Size
Orientation changes the page between Portrait and Landscape. Paper Size selects A4, Letter, Legal, and other sizes.
4. Print Area
Print Area allows only selected cells to be printed instead of the entire worksheet.
5. Headers and Footers
Headers appear at the top of every printed page, while footers appear at the bottom. They usually contain page numbers, file names, dates, or organization names.

body.title: Insert Header & Footer
steps: Add page numbers or dates if required.

body.text: 6. Print Preview
Print Preview allows you to check how the worksheet will appear before printing.

body.title: Open Print Preview
steps: Review the preview window before printing.

body.title: Practice Exercise - Print Ready Report
steps: Add a header with the school name.
Add page numbers in the footer.
